task: Replace distributed prefix-based dispatch inference with one typed, fail-closed agent contract.
outcome: A user runs lattice dispatch for verification-intent, test-intent, or test-case-reviewer with the required itemId and sees a role-specific verification/review prompt with no git commit or checklist status:done instructions; valid story reviewers run without itemId; an unknown type or wrong identifier combination exits nonzero and prints the accepted types and required cardinality.
facts: story-dispatch.ts currently classifies reviewers only by the lattice-review- prefix
dispatch currently permits only three hard-coded story-level agent types
command-catalog agentType guidance says only the INIT reviewer may be story-level, which disagrees with the handler
verification-intent and legacy test aliases can fall into the implementer prompt branch
Workstream C requires a shared registry and explicitly forbids adding more prefix checks

Repository prompt assets define implementer, INIT/product/scope/story reviewers, behavior/concept/quality/docs/channel/test-coverage/delivery reviewers, implementation-reviewer, test-intent and test-case-reviewer roles

Mutation authority is already mechanically enforced in role-sensitive handlers such as checklist, review-run, init-check, scope-check and delivery-check; registry helpers can replace their duplicated role sets/classifiers without redesigning command-policy ownership
docs/requirements/decisions/role-separation.md is the canonical subsystem owner for role separation and must be synchronized with C4 runtime semantics
constraints: Preserve deliberate legacy aliases while removing accidental fallback semantics
Unknown types fail before prompt generation and never receive implementer instructions
Schema, handler, prompt builder, hints, role permissions, and tests consume one contract
Gate-consumed reviewer semantics require process-fact registry and verifier synchronization
Do not absorb host liveness, owner identity, or AST scope workstreams into this story
